name: Lighting and Appearance Models
text:
# Lighting and Appearance Models


## Overview
Lighting and Appearance Models extend the [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) architecture [11313-model-architecture-modifications.md] to explicitly model illumination, material properties, or stylistic variations, rather than predicting view-dependent color directly from position and direction. These methods solve the problem of disentangling geometry from appearance, enabling capabilities such as explicit relighting, [physically-based rendering](#6815-physically-based-rendering-pbr-lighting.md), or controllable style synthesis. They differ from siblings like [DoF-NeRF](9432-dof-nerf.md) by introducing specific parameterizations for light transport or style, rather than focusing on depth-of-field or sparse-view constraints.

## Shared principles
The standard NeRF architecture [11313-model-architecture-modifications.md] learns a continuous volumetric scene representation $F_\Theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$. Lighting and Appearance Models modify this mapping to output intermediate physical or stylistic quantities (e.g., albedo, normal, pre-integrated light, or style vectors) which are then combined with explicit lighting or style conditions during the rendering step. The rendering process still integrates these outputs along rays using [standard volume rendering equations](#1165-standard-volume-rendering-equation.md), but the final color $\mathbf{C}$ is derived from a more complex composition of these intermediate fields and external parameters.

## Subtopics

### [Neural Pre-Integrated Lighting (Neural-PIL)](13783-neural-pre-integrated-lighting-neural-pil.md)
Neural-PIL replaces costly numerical integration of incoming light with a neural network query, predicting pre-integrated light $\tilde{L}_i(\omega_r, b_r)$ directly from an illumination embedding, view direction, and material roughness [13783-neural-pre-integrated-lighting-neural-pil.md]. It sets itself apart from [Spherical Harmonics NeRF](14480-spherical-harmonics-nerf.md) by using an MLP to represent finer illumination details efficiently, avoiding the lack of fine details or high memory costs associated with SH bases [13783-neural-pre-integrated-lighting-neural-pil.md]. Choose this method when physically-based relighting with roughness-dependent specular highlights is required.

### [Spherical Harmonics NeRF](14480-spherical-harmonics-nerf.md)
[Spherical Harmonics NeRF](#14480-spherical-harmonics-nerf.md) replaces the standard view-dependent color prediction head with an explicit 2nd-order [Spherical Harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) (SH) illumination model, allowing for explicit relighting by varying learnable SH coefficients [14480-spherical-harmonics-nerf.md]. It differs from siblings like Neural-PIL by decoupling geometry (density) and appearance (albedo) into separate accumulations, then applying a global, per-image [SH lighting](#11516-spherical-harmonics-lighting-calculation.md) model to the accumulated screen-space albedo and normals, rather than predicting color directly per sample [14480-spherical-harmonics-nerf.md]. Choose this method when global, consistent relighting of a scene is the primary goal.

### StylizedNeRF
[StylizedNeRF](#14882-stylizednerf.md) (also known as StyleNeRF) integrates a style-based generator into the [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) architecture for high-resolution 3D-aware image synthesis [14882-stylizednerf.md]. It solves the problem of generating high-fidelity, view-consistent 3D objects with controllable appearance styles, addressing the limitations of standard NeRF which lacks explicit style conditioning [14882-stylizednerf.md]. It sets itself apart from siblings like Neural-PIL by using a GAN-based mutual learning strategy with a 2D stylization network, rather than optimizing for physical lighting parameters [14882-stylizednerf.md]. Choose this method for artistic style transfer or synthesis of specific subject appearances.

## Background
The baseline NeRF architecture  employs two MLPs: a Position MLP $\Phi_{pos}$ and a Shading MLP $\Phi_{shade}$. Lighting and Appearance Models emerged to address the limitations of this monolithic color prediction, enabling explicit control over lighting and style. Neural-PIL  and Spherical Harmonics NeRF  focus on physical illumination, while StylizedNeRF  focuses on generative style synthesis.
